summary: An excerpt from a fiction work, 'Book 12 — part 27', in which Lexy Moran and Captain Grey talk by the fire. Captain Grey voices a sense of uneasiness he feels, which Lexy urges him to treat as a warning, and then he begins to explain his worries about his younger sister Muriel, whom he has not seen since he was six. The passage ends mid-conversation as he recounts their family history and the failed plan for her to join him in England.
one_line: Lexy Moran and Captain Grey discuss his feelings of uneasiness and his long-estranged sister Muriel by the fire.
key_facts: Lexy Moran and Captain Grey talk by the firelight, and Lexy finds his face sensitive and fine rather than haughty.
Captain Grey says he has a feeling that something is wrong and asks whether one should laugh at it or take it as a warning.
Lexy replies that feelings like that are a warning and that it is foolish and wrong to disregard them.
Captain Grey says he has been trying to tell himself he is an utter ass, but he knows there is something wrong.
Lexy feels an unreasoning dread when he hints at something serious and briefly does not want to hear more.
Captain Grey says the matter concerns his sister, Muriel.
Captain Grey last saw Muriel when he was six years old and she was a baby.
Muriel's mother died when Muriel was born, out in India.
An aunt took Muriel to the States, and Captain Grey stayed out there with his father.
Muriel is twenty-one years old, and Captain Grey's last picture of her shows her at about fourteen.
Captain Grey describes Muriel as a pretty kid, a bit more than pretty, and lovely.
While Captain Grey was at school in England, it was arranged for Muriel to come over, but she did not, and they have never met again.
Captain Grey says twenty-one years is a long time since they last met.
